messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Setting/mapping x/y
parts:
Some confusing things about mapping vs. setting:

df <- data.frame(a=1:10)

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a))

OK, this is exactly as expected.

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a,colour="blue"))

OK, this is exactly as expected.  The constant "blue" is being *mapped*, and displays as red.

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a,colour=13:14))  (or factor(13:14))

OK, this is mapping 13:14 to two colors, blue and red.

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a,colour=13))

Strange, this should be mapping the constant 13 to a constant color, I'd think, but in fact there is no plotting at all, and the scale is named "13" with a value of 14 represented as ... nothing.

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a,colour=13:14))

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a),colour="blue")

OK, exactly as expected.  The color is being set to blue.

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a),y=23)

Strange, this gives an error (apply non-function).  Shouldn't this be 'setting' y to 23?

ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=23))

This works, though.

          -s

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Setting/mapping x/y
parts:
Haldey will be the only one with a definitive answer to this but this
is my understanding:

> ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a,colour=13))
>
> Strange, this should be mapping the constant 13 to a constant color,
> I'd think, but in fact there is no plotting at all, and the scale is
> named "13" with a value of 14 represented as ... nothing.

My guess is that it interprets 13 as a color specification and 13 is
not a valid one so there is no color. How exactly the color is
interpreted depends on grid and the help of gpar reads:

Colours can be specified in one of the forms returned by 'rgb', as
a name (see 'colors') or as a positive integer index into the
current palette (with zero or negative values being taken as
transparent).

However
ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a,colour=1)
gives the same result even though:
palette()
[1] "black" "red" "green3" "blue" "cyan" "magenta" "yellow"
[8] "gray"
i.e. palette()[1] exists.

So maybe ggplot is doing something with the color in between.

> ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a),y=23)
>
> Strange, this gives an error (apply non-function). Shouldn't this
> be 'setting' y to 23?
>
> ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=23))
>
> This works, though.

This is probably because x and y and *required* aesthetics (as opposed
to colour etc. which can be only parameters). But I agree with you,
the first form should work and is more coherent with the concepts in
ggplot (well my understanding of them at least).
Actually, I think the second form even used to be invalid. At least
this construct:
foo=23
ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=foo))
used to be invalid for sure. To map something, you *had* to put in the
data frame specified by the data argument. This indeed made sense from
the grammar point of view (but the current behavior is often more
practical).

I hope that helps a bit.

JiHO

This is a bug with the default colour scale for numeric data - the
colour gradient. Obviously with only one point it can't figure out
how to create the gradient.

> ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a,colour=13:14))
>
> ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a,y=a),colour="blue")
>

>
> ggplot(data=df) + geom_point(aes(x=a),y=23)
>
> Strange, this gives an error (apply non-function).  Shouldn't this be
> 'setting' y to 23?

Yes. Currently most of the code assumes that x and y are mapped, but
I will look at this again.
